design_condition: The orthogonal comb occupies the southern plot between the historic complex and the city, using alternating courtyards and building arms to improve permeability and create differentiated public, semi-private, and intimate outdoor spaces.

positive.statement: The comb structure creates an interesting spatial transition between the historic enclosure and the existing city.

position.rationale: Comb massing and alternating arms are clearly legible across the footprint and elevations.

positive.statement: The orthogonal placement facilitates north-south permeability and establishes a hierarchy of external spaces and circulation.

position.rationale: Longitudinal gaps between arms suggest permeability through the central and southern open spaces.

positive.statement: The sequence of built bodies and courtyards successfully reproduces the dimensions of the existing spaces.

position.target: sequence of built bodies and courtyards
position.rationale: Repeated courtyard voids and orthogonal building segments are visible in the top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The differentiation of public spaces, including more intimate residential areas, is an important quality.

position.target: differentiated public and intimate residential spaces
position.rationale: Open courtyard regions provide plausible locations for differentiated public and intimate outdoor spaces.

positive.statement: The housing typologies are well studied, and the variation of modules is convincing.

position.rationale: Repeated segmented arms and varied bay patterns indicate modular housing organization.

positive.statement: The greenery and paths remain continuous through the enclosure and connect the river with the school garden.

position.rationale: Courtyard and perimeter gaps offer approximate routes through the comb, though landscape is not distinguishable.

positive.statement: The urban forest positively affects the microclimate and filters emissions from the surrounding road.

position.rationale: A peripheral southern-western open area is used as a plausible landscape anchor.

positive.statement: The green roof and insulated load-bearing structure are effective choices.

position.target: green roof and insulated load-bearing structure
position.rationale: The upper envelope is visible, while roof planting and insulation remain unresolved in the sample.

negative.statement: The relationship between the base and upper part of the new volume is unconvincing.

position.target: base and upper part of new volume
position.rationale: Layered lower and upper masses are visible in the elevations across the building.

negative.statement: The distribution and accesses are ambiguous, with consequences for the façades.

position.rationale: Likely access points occur along southern courtyard-facing edges, but entrances are not individually identifiable.

negative.statement: The different connections between the comb arms and central body create an inconsistency between courtyards.

position.target: connections between comb arms and central body
position.rationale: Junctions between repeated arms and the central body are visible as varied courtyard connections.

negative.statement: The distribution system is spatially interesting but rather complicated.

position.rationale: The segmented plan suggests complexity, but internal circulation is not directly represented.

negative.statement: The relevance of opening skylights in the existing roof is questioned.

position.rationale: A roof-level point is assigned within the northern upper envelope, though skylights are not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The relationship with the historical complex is not entirely convincing.

position.rationale: The northern edge is used as the interface toward the stated historical complex.

negative.statement: The execution methods require better verification given the complex geometry.

position.rationale: The full segmented envelope provides the spatial anchor for construction complexity.

negative.statement: Summer thermal comfort and cooling needs, especially in glazed common areas, must be checked.

position.target: summer thermal comfort in glazed common areas
position.rationale: A courtyard-facing mid-height zone is a plausible location for glazed common areas.

negative.statement: The treatment of systems in the existing buildings is less in-depth.

position.rationale: The northern-western building edge is used as an approximate existing-building systems anchor.
